documents.title: Charge to Academic Programs on Generative AI in Instructional Settings
documents.summary: The provost's 2023 charge asks every academic unit to write its own unit-specific guidance on generative AI, recommends working with rather than against AI, and suggests scaffolding restrictions by course level. It sets no stance of its own.
documents.stance_why: It says "each discipline and academic unit will need to consider" and asks "every academic unit develop long-term, unit-specific guidance", handing the stance to units, so delegates.

units.why: The provost says "each discipline and academic unit will need to consider" impacts in its own context, so the decision sits with units; P04 (who sets the rule) fits better than P56 because no framework is given.
units.anchor: each discipline and academic unit will need to consider the potential impacts

units.why: MSU "recommends that academic units seek ways to work with, not in opposition to, generative AI", a recommendation leaning toward embracing AI, so default-permit/encourage (P02).
units.anchor: seek ways to work with, not in opposition to, generative AI

units.why: The Strategic Plan goal to "prepare its students, educators, researchers, and community for success" in a changing professional landscape is a career-readiness rationale (P44), stated as fact.
units.anchor: prepare its students, educators, researchers, and community for success
units.policy: MSU's 2030 Strategic Plan goals include preparing students, educators, researchers and the community for success in an ever-changing academic and professional landscape, which is the stated reason units should work with generative AI.

units.why: "asks that every academic unit develop long-term, unit-specific guidance" is a charge to units to set their own instructor-facing guidance, so P04 (rule set at unit level) rather than P09 (syllabus statement).
units.anchor: every academic unit develop long-term, unit-specific guidance for its instructors

units.why: "what is acceptable, or even preferred, in some units might be antithetical to other units' values" explains why no single rule is set; a statement about who decides (P04).
units.anchor: what is acceptable, or even preferred, in some units might be antithetical
units.policy: MSU recognizes that what is acceptable, or even preferred, in some units might be antithetical to other units' values.

units.why: Units are asked to take "scaffolding a policy based on course level (i.e., more restrictions at the 100-level to more options at the 400-level)" into account; permission staged by course level matches P08.
units.anchor: scaffolding a policy based on course level (i.e., more restrictions at the 100-level to more
units.policy: Unit policies take into consideration scaffolding a policy based on course level, with more restrictions at the 100-level and more options at the 400-level.

units.why: The unit policy must account for "the diverse teaching modalities in the unit" and "forms of assessment"; this tells units to vary rules by setting, so it is P04 (rule varies by activity) not P08, which is level-specific.
units.anchor: takes into consideration the diverse teaching modalities in the unit
units.policy: Unit policies take into consideration the diverse teaching modalities in the unit, forms of assessment, teaching loads and class sizes.

units.why: Asking units to "consider if your unit needs to adopt or alter an honor code or pledge" is a policy action about integrity pledges that no listed type covers.
units.anchor: Consider if your unit needs to adopt or alter an honor code or pledge
units.uncovered_note: Units consider adopting or altering an honor code or pledge in light of generative AI.

units.why: "Determine if a common AI technology needs to be adopted department-wide" concerns a unit-wide sanctioned tool, which is P17.
units.anchor: Determine if a common AI technology needs to be adopted department-wide

units.why: "Develop a process to review your policy/guidance to stay abreast of advances in the technology" is a review-cycle requirement (P54).
units.anchor: Develop a process to review your policy/guidance to stay abreast of advances

units.why: "Review and modify your courses' curriculum design, learning outcomes, assessment, and/or assignments" ties course redesign to the AI policy, so P35.
units.anchor: Review and modify your courses’ curriculum design, learning outcomes, assessment, and/or assignments

units.why: Pointing units to the "Code of Teaching Responsibility, Integrity of Scholarship and Grades" as sources of guidance sets the existing integrity framework as the base (P56), not a stance.
units.anchor: units can also find guidance from existing MSU policies including the Code of Teaching Responsibility

units.why: CTLI and EDLI "will be producing resources, offering workshops, and facilitating discussions" to support faculty, which matches P63.
units.anchor: will be producing resources, offering workshops, and facilitating discussions throughout the year

documents.title: MSU Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI Tools
documents.summary: MSU's 2025 university-wide guidelines require instructors to put an AI statement in every syllabus and say students may use AI only when the instructor permits. They also cover research, administrative work, data protection and the handling of suspected misuse. Instructors and units set the substantive rules.
documents.stance_why: The guideline says "Instructors are expected to establish a course-specific guidance" and "Students may only use generative AI tools ... when explicitly permitted by the instructor"; the rule for students is set by each instructor, so delegates.

notes: No school- or computing-level documents or course documents were collected for Michigan State. The CTLI guide states that MSU has no university-wide classroom AI policy, while the 2025 provost guidelines state an official framework; the two documents differ in date. Example statements in the CTLI guide come from other universities and MSU instructors; they were coded as units because the guide presents them as models. Exact repeats of the template boilerplate across restrict/permit/require statements were coded once.
